feature_definitions.f_slope300: least-squares slope of x over k-299..k, times 300 samples, / s[k]
feature_definitions.f_identical_run: log(1 + number of consecutive identical readings ending at k)
feature_definitions.f_frac_zero_d1_30: fraction of zero first differences over k-29..k
feature_definitions.f_frac_zero_d1_300: fraction of zero first differences over k-329..k-30 (past baseline)

run_info.noise_scale: s[k] = max( 1.4826*median(|d1| over k-60..k-1)/sqrt(2), 1.2533*mean(|d1| over k-60..k-1)/sqrt(2), floor ), floor = 0.25 * median(raw s) over fault-free calibration-partition records of the measurand
run_info.disclaimer: Synthetic data only; no physical sensor accuracy is claimed.

temperature_transient_investigation.summary: **Temperature transients.** Highest conventional false-alarm rates by scenario/phase (test): TEMP_PLATEAUS/plateau_settling: conventional 22.6 %, GBT 1.3 %, IF 0.0 % (n=1200); TEMP_RAMPS/hold_end: conventional 20.0 %, GBT 0.8 %, IF 0.0 % (n=120); FD_TEMP_COMMUNICATION_GAP/plateau_settling: conventional 19.3 %, GBT 6.9 %, IF 0.0 % (n=347); FD_TEMP_ABRUPT_CHANGE/plateau_settling: conventional 18.6 %, GBT 0.0 %, IF 0.0 % (n=371); FD_TEMP_NON_FINITE/plateau_settling: conventional 17.6 %, GBT 1.0 %, IF 0.0 % (n=397). The conventional per-segment MAD treats each ramp or post-step lag segment as if it were a stationary level, so the trend itself exceeds the MAD threshold; the causal ML features normalise by a past first-difference noise scale, which a smooth ramp does not inflate.

baseline_estimation_diagnostics.interpretation: sigma and target are estimated from a short baseline window (60-180 samples); estimation error in either reduces the true in-control ARL by orders of magnitude relative to the nominal Siegmund value, which is why h well above the nominal design value is needed for zero false alarms.

milestone2_nine_controls.note: 6 of these 9 runs are in the calibration/validation partitions and were part of the tuning set; only the 3 test-partition controls are independent.

verdict: - voltage_V: macro event recall (test) GBT 0.71, IF 0.24, conventional 0.38; record FAR GBT 0.0127, IF 0.0058, conventional 0.0038. Highest event recall: Gradient-boosted trees.
- current_mA: macro event recall (test) GBT 0.47, IF 0.45, conventional 0.58; record FAR GBT 0.0039, IF 0.0054, conventional 0.0121. Highest event recall: Conventional per-segment.
- temperature_C: macro event recall (test) GBT 0.39, IF 0.51, conventional 0.56; record FAR GBT 0.0088, IF 0.0053, conventional 0.0511. Highest event recall: Conventional per-segment.
- CUSUM: tuned configuration 1/39 false alarms and 8/9 drift runs detected on test, versus 39/39 false alarms for the existing configuration.
- Statements of superiority apply only to these synthetic test runs and the documented fault model; small event counts (2–10 per class per measurand) give wide uncertainty on every recall figure.
limitations: All data are synthetic; the fault generator and the detectors share the same simulated noise model, which favours learned detectors.
Event counts per class and measurand in the test partition are small (2 for persistent classes, 4–10 for transient classes); a 95 % interval on a recall of 2/2 spans roughly 0.16–1.0.
Offset, gain and drift faults are fundamentally ambiguous from a single DUT signal (indistinguishable from genuine process changes); detection near onset relies on the step/slope signature only.
Stuck temperature signals are partly unobservable because coarse quantisation makes identical consecutive readings normal on plateaus.
Thresholds are set for a 0.5 % validation false-alarm rate; test FAR can differ, and other operating points trade recall for false alarms.
The conventional baseline uses protocol segment boundaries and non-causal per-segment statistics; it is not an online detector.
The CUSUM error series uses the reference instrument and a static calibration; it is a laboratory-verification setting, not reference-free field monitoring.
The ML models are research artefacts; they are not integrated into the application or the R1–R5 decision engine.
